title: "Feature Extraction"
description: "The transformation of raw inputs into a set of informative representations or measurements."
term: "Feature Extraction"
letter: "F"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Feature extraction converts raw inputs into a smaller or more useful set
of measurements that a model can process. The features may be designed
by people or learned by another model.

## Technical explanation

An extraction function maps input data $x$ to features $z=f(x)$. Classical
methods may compute explicit descriptors, while deep-learning encoders
learn representations from examples. Extractors can be fixed or trained
jointly with a downstream model.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Raw data may be high-dimensional, noisy, or difficult for a downstream
model to use directly. Feature extraction can improve efficiency and
expose task-relevant structure, but may discard information needed for
other tasks.

## How it works

A transformation analyzes an input and produces measurements or
representations. These outputs are passed to a classifier, retrieval
system, or other downstream component. If the extractor is learned, its
training data and version must be tracked.

## Practical example

A pretrained image encoder can turn each photo into a vector. A smaller
classifier can use these vectors to distinguish categories without
training the entire image model from scratch.

## Common misconceptions

- Feature extraction and feature selection are different: extraction
  transforms data, while selection chooses among existing features.
- Extracted features are not automatically interpretable or useful.
- Fitting an extractor using evaluation data can leak information.
